captureVars.name: updatesSyncToken
captureVars.description: x-ms-synctoken for api/csa users/me/updates. The value the real client sends rolls forward with the wall clock, so a hardcoded token freezes the sync window; the response hands back the next one at .metadata.syncToken. A firehose capture corpus buries an updates response fast — the sidebar refresh is minutes apart while the corpus grows continuously — so this typically needs `mcx site capture teams --limit 2000` or deeper. While uncaptured, applyVarHeaders drops the header rather than sending an unresolved ${…}.

captureVars.name: me_mri
captureVars.description: Own Teams MRI, '8:orgid:' + AAD object id. Bound as $vars.me_mri so response transforms can compute is_me / mentions_me, and used as the default subject for user_fetch. Read from the x-ms-object-id request header when present, else from the Bearer JWT's oid claim (base64url re-padded before @base64d) — the JWT rides nearly every api/chatsvc|csa|mt request, the header only a handful.
captureVars.jq:
(.requestHeaders["x-ms-object-id"] // "" | strings) as $hdr
| (if ($hdr | length) == 36 then $hdr else
     (.requestHeaders.authorization // "" | strings | sub("^[Bb]earer +";"") | split(".") | (.[1] // "")
      | select(length > 0)
      | (. | gsub("-";"+") | gsub("_";"/")) as $b
      | ($b + (("=" * ((4 - ($b | length % 4)) % 4)) // ""))
      | @base64d | fromjson | .oid | strings)
   end)
| select(length == 36) | "8:orgid:" + .
